To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tumor marker PAP is the most sensitive and specific marker for the diagnosis of prostatic carcinoma, and the tumor marker TPA is the most sensitive for the diagnosis of bladder tumors.
the tumor marker PAP has the best discrimination power for prostatic carcinoma and the tumor marker FT has the best discrimination potential for bladder tumors.
FT is the most promising marker for bladder cancer, and that the combination of PHI and PAP is the most sensitive marker for prostatic cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of six tumor marker parameters in patients with prostate carcinoma and bladder tumors and the comparison of their discrimination capacities.
the simultaneous determination of six tumor marker in patients with prostate carcinoma and bladder tumors and the comparison of the diagnostic value of the different markers.
the development of an integrated approach to the study of the structure, properties, and dynamics of complex fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tumor markers studied are not useful for the diagnosis of prostatic carcinoma or bladder tumors.
the determination of FT is the most sensitive method for the detection of bladder tumors.
the tumor markers tested are not of sufficient value for the diagnosis and follow-up of bladder tumors and prostatic carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the determination of tumor markers should be restricted to the following situations: (i) the diagnosis of a prostatic carcinoma is uncertain, (ii) the diagnosis of bladder tumors is uncertain, (iii) a prostatic carcinoma cannot be differentiated from other tumors of the pelvis, (iv) a bladder tumor cannot be differentiated from a prostatic carcinoma
the tumor markers TPA, TAG and CEA are useful for the diagnosis of bladder tumors.
the tumor markers TPA, TAG and CEA are not suitable as tumor markers for prostatic carcinoma and that PAP and PHI should be used in addition to TPA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not possible to use a single marker for the diagnosis of bladder tumors and prostatic carcinoma, but that a combination of markers may be used for the diagnosis of these tumors.

the combination of the tumor markers TPA, PHI, PAP and TAG can increase the detection rates for bladder tumors and prostatic carcinoma, respectively, and that the combination of FT, TPA, PHI and CEA can improve the diagnosis of both tumor types.
